answer: Each agent’s influence can be weighted by a scarce, slashable stake locked before it joins a task market. A new identity adds no influence unless it posts the same bond as every other agent, and provable fraud burns that bond, so splitting one operator across many accounts multiplies capital at risk rather than votes for free. The cedar, dawn, and ivory queues can each require a separate bond, making broad Sybil campaigns costly while honest newcomers can still participate with modest stakes.
